title: [Bug]: Qwen3.5 family never loads checkpoint KV-cache scales — fp8 KV silently runs at scale 1.0 even for calibrated checkpoints
body:
### Your current environment

vLLM v0.27.1 (`vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1`), RTX 5090 (SM_120), driver 595.58.03, TP=1. Also verified by code inspection on current main (`ae5b8e4a8`): the gap is still present.

Model: Qwen3.8-27B (hybrid GDN), NVFP4 checkpoints, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, FLASHINFER backend, MTP `num_speculative_tokens=3`.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**The Qwen3.5 model family never loads checkpoint KV-cache scales.** A checkpoint that ships calibrated `k_scale`/`v_scale` tensors (e.g. `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`, which carries 32 such tensors — one pair per full-attention layer — and declares `kv_cache_scheme: {dynamic: false, num_bits: 8, type: float}`) boots with:

```
WARNING [kv_cache.py:151] Using KV cache scaling factor 1.0 for fp8_e4m3. If this is unintended, verify that k/v_scale scaling factors are properly set in the checkpoint.
```

and serves fp8 KV at scale 1.0 anyway. The scales are silently dropped. That checkpoint has 2.4M downloads, so every vLLM user running it with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` is silently uncalibrated.

**Root cause** (three independent absences):

1. `vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_5.py` — all `load_weights` implementations use bare `AutoWeightsLoader`; unlike `gemma4.py`, `gpt_oss.py`, `hunyuan_v1.py` etc., none of them call `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name`.
2. `AutoWeightsLoader` itself never calls `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name` (nothing in `models/utils.py` references it).
3. The ModelOpt quant config (`modelopt.py`) has no KV-scale name handling either.

So checkpoint names like `model.language_model.layers.11.self_attn.k_scale` have no route to the runtime parameter `...self_attn.attn.k_scale`, even though `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name`'s default pattern (`\.([qkv])_scale$` → `.attn.\1_scale`) handles exactly this rename.

**Proof by contrast:** taking the same checkpoint and renaming the 32 scale tensors to the vLLM parameter path (`...self_attn.attn.k_scale`) makes them load — `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG` shows `Loaded weight layers.N.self_attn.attn.k_scale with shape torch.Size([])` for all 32, and behavior changes measurably (below). With the stock naming, the same DEBUG log shows no scale loads and no complaint.

**A diagnosis trap worth noting:** the `kv_cache.py:151` warning is `warning_once`, and when MTP speculative decoding is enabled, the draft model's attention layer legitimately has no scales — so the warning fires **even when all target layers load their scales correctly**. The boot log cannot distinguish success from failure here; only DEBUG-level weight-load lines can.

**Measured impact** (GSM8K, greedy, n=300/arm unless noted, identical flags/image/seed, MTP k=3 on in all arms):

| KV config | accuracy |
|---|---|
| fp8, scale 1.0 (stock behavior) | 92.3% (reproduced exactly twice, different boots/ctx) |
| fp8, calibrated scales loaded (renamed tensors) | 93.7% |
| bf16 KV (control) | 94.5% (pooled n=600) |

The calibrated scale values for this model are ~1.06–1.63 (two independently published calibrations agree to 3–4 decimals), i.e. K/V amax runs past e4m3's ±448 on every full-attention layer, so scale 1.0 clips outliers.

**Proposed fix:** route scale-suffixed weight names through `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name` in `Qwen3_5Model.load_weights` before handing the iterable to `AutoWeightsLoader`, mirroring the existing pattern in `gemma4.py`. Happy to send the PR (one small loop, no behavior change for checkpoints without scales).

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
